This game touts itself as being a metroidvania 3D game but honestly it has nothing of the genre. It's a 3D, character changer puzzler with shooter elements. Think 3rd person Gobliiins with guns.
I have a limited amount of playtime on Steam, but keep it mind I had the game on Desura from my previous purchase and had played it before.
The game is still in early alpha and it shows, very much. Controls and movements are sluggish, graphics are very bland and sterile (the washed out cell shading effect doesn't do it for me), and in my case the game wouldn't even start without completely deactivating audio. The default controls aren't well thought of either and you will find yourself frustratingly deactivating panels while trying to change character. You are thrown into the game with no real explanation but a few engrish lines of text as you go on, teaching you the bare minimum. The atmosphere felt dull, and I got no real entertainment factor. There's a reason no one is playing the game, including those who provided such good reviews.
I understand that the game is currently in Early Access, actually it has been in alpha state for nearly 3 years, and I'd be happy to revisit this review if I'm told that any significant improvement has been made regarding these issues.
There's also the fact that communications between the developers and the community has been less than stellar, their choice of providing only a subset of their previous customers with a Steam copy of the game they bought, and deleting negative comments on both Steam's community hub and the Desura game page. (Some of those comments were downright nasty but there was also legitimate criticism that got deleted.)

If you want to pay $20 for an unfinished game that looks like it belongs on Dreamcast, here's your chance. Don't get me wrong, I'm not a big graphics guy. I can easily dig a good game with retro style graphics like Shovel Knight that pays good homage to its era. In comparison, TBC just looks dated (gaming circa 2002) and has probably the ugliest use of cel shading I've ever seen. The game's atmosphere feels sterile void of any charm or interest. And the audio? Completely forgettable, I don't remember a single tune from the game, granted most of the playtime is with the Desura build so this may have changed with the Steam release but from my brief testing, the game appears unchanged from its most recent build on Desura.
The gameplay isn't much better. The controls are ultra clunky and the combat reminds me slightly of the old PS2/XBox horror game Cold Fear but have action games come a long way since then and honestly Cold Fear already did it better. The puzzles are easy and occasionally well crafted but don't feel substantial enough to carry the game. It feels like the game was trying to be a mix of something cerebral like Portal and while having action similar to Resident Evil 4 but fell completely flat in both regards.   If a developer is going to price their game at the level of some of the 2 year old AAA games, it should be able to hold its own. No, I'm not expecting AAA quality from an indie developer, but the pricing falls in the premium range as far as indie products go therfore I expect something good. This game is far from the indie cream of the crop. TBC fails miserably in many areas and it's simply just not fun to play.
I'm glad I won my copy in the winter auction for far less than the regular price. At regular price, the game is far too boring and unpolished to be worth the $$$. There's some honest hard effort evident in this game but good effort is not enough reason to give a recommendation. At least, the game seems to launch more stable in its Steam release, I had to jump through hoops to get the game to simply load through Desura. In comparison I tried loading the game 3 times in Steam and it loaded perfectly each time.
(Removed segment about developers and distributing keys to bundle buyers. They eventually gave keys to the Groupees bundle buyers)
Keep in mind this is an Early Access game, things could improve in the future and if they do improve I will be willing to re-visit the game and change my recommendation if the game warrants it. As it remains now, the game is a mess and not one I can recommend.

Let's start with a note: In the description the game claims to be a Metroidvania. This makes no sense, at all.
This game is not a metroidvania so don't be fooled by that, while there are rooms connected between each other that's not what makes a game a metroidvania in ANY WAY.
This game it's an action adventure full of puzzles and with a funny (even if not that innovative to be honest) mechanic, you can swap your body between human like manikins to resolve puzzles and go further in your adventure.
Your mission it's to depure a scientific plant.
And this is all about the story for now, let's talk more about the game, shall we?
Graphically the game does not offer anything special, the enemy models are color swaps of the same 4 so no variety under this aspect and the scenarios textures are almost nonexistent, of course this could be the developers' choice after all.
The musics tracks are few and you are probably going to easily forget there's any music at all, aside for the "battle theme" wich is a 10 seconds theme repeated until the battle ends, really.
Story wise the game does not offer anything special, sure it's still in alpha stage but i expected something more than "you are there to fix the mess, bye", after all this is adventure game and the story, at least in my opinion, is really important.
Controls are really messy sometimes and the aiming is a real problem, you get no crosshair aside for the "laser" but that does not help that much, maybe that's just a matter of practice but when you are doing the "light balls" puzzles not knowing where you are actually aiming makes these puzzles really frustrating sometimes.
The dodge is basically a barrel roll and after a patch you can do it pressing left or right two times, surely easier than before.
That and the realoading wich makes you really slow for like 3 seconds makes some battles really hard (and it's not a bad thing) and frustrating in some cases (and this is bad).
Puzzles are really easy, in fact the only way to waste time on it is to die because of some glitch (like the deaths sometimes happen in the "mirror rooms") or because enemies hit your uncontrolled character throwing it into the red water killing it without any way to save it, sure you need to be alert so maybe it's just a way to punish you if you get distracted, maybe.
You can't save your game whenever you want, the game saves automatically so if the save it's far away from the point of your death... well you got the idea right?
I guess this is another discutible choice, not everyone loves such a thing in fact.
The map it's so small and there's no way to enlarge it and this makes it. most of the time, completely useless.
This is my opinion (for now) about The Body Changer, the game is still in alpha but, to be honest, i haven't seen much changes from the old alpha.
The game has been released for less than a week on Steam so the developers have plenty of time to fix some things still, for now and for the price asked, this game it's a No for me.
If you still want to buy it you have to know about something, the game does not have an ending yet, infact when you get to the fifth depurator you can't go further (and that's half of the game).
So yes you are paying for half of game for now.
This is all I've got to say for now, i'm probably going to change my review if something big changes or maybe when the game comes out of Early Access just in case.
Until then.

I wanted to like this game. I really did. It takes place in amazing environments, the characters seem interesting enough, and the story seems interesting as well. But, frankly, the gameplay is terrible, mainly because of the ridiculously awful camera controls. It doesn't matter if you are using a gamepad or kb/m, the game has it's own ideas about what it wants to do with the camera and it will fight your control of it every step of the way.
The worst is in combat, where the camera will often shift angles automatically, usually to angles more about making your character look cool than about actually giving you a decent view of or angle of attack on your enemies. Many times this stupidity will cause your attacks to go completely in the wrong direction, which really sucks for charged attacks.
Seriously, it's just not fun when you have to fight the camera just as much as you fight the bad guys, and you have to do so while trying to fight the bad guys.
If the camera were better under user control without the game randomly shifting it around based on whatever automatic rules it follows, then I would probably be willing to recommend this game. But as it is now, with utter crap camera control making combat pretty much impossible, or at least insanely frustrating, at times, I cannot recommend this game.

I highly recommend this game. What stood out to me the most is that I didn't see the repeatitive copying of items, floor layouts, or cloned npc's (minus the robots). The station looked lived in. Each area felt unique and that it had a purpose or logic to it. Overall, the layout, the ambience, lighting, sounds and feel of the environment is the best I've ever seen in a sci-fi game.
An add bonus for me was when I bought the game I had an ok/older graphics card (it was like a radeon 6670 2gb ddr3). The game still looked beautiful on low settings.
The noise and sounds of the game... emerges you into the environment (recommend head phones for intensifying game experience). Sounds ranging from something metallic dropping in the distance and the droning hum of the station to the alien stalking you in the air vents.
Gameplay: Its a stealth/survival type game. It has elements of crafting, some combat if you get caught, small puzzle/problem solving situations. The alien AI will adapt to your habits of hiding so don't always go for the wall locker or rolling cabinet. There is more than one path to get around obsticals undetected... which can make it easier to remain undetected but may be the end of you if you linger to long.
Tip: USE THE LEAN ACTION! If your crouched behind an object you better be leaning against a wall or said object. Line of sight will get you 9 out of 10 but if your leaning you have an extremely higher chance of not being seen from peripheral vision.
You have a few moments in the game where you can move about the station freely without stiring unwanted attention. Thankfully it isn't limited to the beginning of the game.

The Alien AI is probably the best AI in a game yet. Instead of cheap pre-scripted scares the real tension and horror comes from being hunted by the Alien. The way it behaves and looks for you is extremely stressful and it even seems to grow smarter as the game goes on, learning from its mistakes and what tactics you have used against it in the past. You are never truly safe from the Alien. I actually managed to hide under tables for the whole game and thought it was a "safe tactic", but once, very late in the game the Alien managed to spot me all the same, lunged under and bit my head off. Alien Isolation has without a doubt some of the best graphics to date.

For fans of Scott's seminal 'Alien', a must. Attemtps ardently to evoke the retro-futurism and grimy schtick of late-70s sci-fi  with great success. Beautiful to look at, atmospheric. Unbelievable sound design. Well optimised. I really love the control scheme - leaning around corners or cover is encouraged, and necessary.
The first four or five hours on Sevastopol station are credible and tense; once introduced, the xenomorph is frightening and ominous. Never have I felt so
as a player character. The level design during these hours is complicated, and there are many places to hide, although not all are safe. Playng cat and mouse with the alien is dynamic and arresting. Unfortunately as the game progresses and the need to conceal one's self lessens, the level design becomes less intricate, populated with human and android obstacles that never match the unpredictability and cunning of the xenomorph AI.
The plot is simplistic, and can be surmised as 'You're stuck on a deteriorating space station, stalked by psychotic androids and a terrifying pradator. Do find a way out, much. And any traces of your mum's lost vessel, those are good too.' Viewed from this distance I was able to pleasantly engage in the simulation of being imprisoned and looking for a way out, piecing together and gathering what tools I could. Ripley's search for her mother takes a back seat, regrettably, and I do wish more was made of this - the imperative which beckoned her to Sevastopol in the first place. Going out of her way to discover recordings from the Nostromo's crew seems completely at odds with the primal instinct to find the nearest exit.
I enjoyed embodying Ripley as a scared but resilient engineer with a good dose of humanity, and whilst the late game's devolution into sparser designs and less exciting enemy encounters hamper the game, I strongly recommend it.

Compared to other big MOBAs and ARTs out there, SMITE is one of the 3 well established giants in the industry. It is more casual than Dota with fewer complex mechanics and being more user friendly and easier to get into. Compared to LoL I would say this game is more immersive. It is much more fun (in my opinion) with a much bigger percentage of characters being viable and fitting the 'meta'. SMITE's lore is really interesting too, it being based on Gods and Immortals from different mythologies and it curious how Hi-Rez mixes all the pantheons together.
Gameplay-wise there are 7 gamemodes as of now, so plenty to play and choose from. Conquest - the traditional 5v5 map with 3 lanes and jungle. Joust - 3v3 with one lane and smaller number of jungle camps. Arena - 5v5 in a colosseum with one wave of creeps marching down and the win condition being ticket based. Assault - another common gamemode with all-random God selection and one lane and no fountain to return to (similar to ARAM in LoL). Clash - 5v5 with 2 lanes and I really don't know what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on in this one. Siege - 4v4 with 2 lanes and jungle in the middle. MOTD - Match of the day, chosen by the devs themselves, this gamemode can be ridiculous or boring, it can be 5v5 of the same God with max money or just a vanilla gamemode, but with cooldown reductions. Overall, you will never be bored with such a range of casual gamemodes in addition to ranked Conquest, Joust and Duel.
This is a fun game, better with friends, you can play casually or try-hard. There are regular patches and events, and new Gods being released almost monthly.
P.S. Invest into an All-Gods pack if you decided to play the game long term, it saves you a lot of money with every month as you get new Gods at their release.

I've played most of the free MOBAs out there, save one Heroes of The Storm. I simply refuse to touch it or any other MOBA after finding this gem.
To start from the beginning, I was avoiding MOBAs quite a bit at first. Having a game simply revolved around 2 teams of players beating the everloving hell out of each other seemed pointless to me at first, but it was soon that I would try DOTA2 - and find out that these games have a certain charm to them that make them entertaining to watch and play. Much like how sports-fanatics religiously watch football, basketball, etc, MOBAs are as such to the people of the internet who love watching fantasy heroes beat the hell out of each other.
It was also with this that I learned where the toxic wastes of the internet thrive, as MOBAs tend to have huge pools of crude, cruel, salty trolls, the most toxic people to exist. You can't join one game without finding anywhere between 2-5 people who can't help but call you any of the worst things on the planet and demanding you to kill yourself in a fire.
Enough about those toxic cesspools though because it was this little gem, SMITE, that gave me insight that not all MOBAs are filled with the worst kind of people in internet history. There are people you just want to kill yes, but it's a huge decline in toxicity compared to most MOBAs (in comparison to DOTA 2 90% less cyanide is being ingested daily when playing SMITE).
The game itself is brilliant in every aspect of the word, while majority of MOBAs have you at a top-down visual and using your mouse to 100% control the character you choose, SMITE allows you to not only control the God you select, but become them, and using every aspect of their ability with the precision and skill they require to be good with them. The game is also 100% totally free, not requiring you to access any form of paywalls for any of the content. Gems, the current cash-like currency, is free to gain in the game through events, promotions, and daily logins, as well as through referring and playing with friends.  All Gods can be obtained with Gems or Favor earned through gameplay, as well as all skins and costumes in the game. The only thing using real world money will do is get you the Gods and skins faster.
Revisiting the community subject, the community in SMITE is very close together. You have a few bad eggs and salty trolls here and there, but as I said before in comparison to other MOBAs, or any MMO for that matter, the number is relatively low, and you can happily play most games without overdosing on your daily sodium intake.
The controls are very intuitive, in my experience, including Keyboard/Mouse and Gamepad support and allowing for easy gameplay no matter what kind of game peripherals you're used to. I personally play with Keyboard and Mouse, as that is what I'm used to using for precision aiming, which brings me to the gameplay mechanics. In many Mobas aiming is as easy as pointing and clicking on the ground or another player, but in SMITE you are expected to be able to aim properly with most abilities. Eat your heart out LoL's Ezreal. This game requires you to pay attention and aim your shots wisely. Some require less skill than others (Kukulkan's Whirlwind), while others require you to line them up nicely for a good result (Neith's Spirit Arrow). There are no ingame boosts to get you ahead of the game's curve or "Pay 2 Win" systems - SMITE wants you to experience the entire game for what it is at its fullest. For that, I give Hi-Rez studio an amazingly large thumbs-up.
Wrapping up this long read of a review, I totally recommend this game to anyone who has an interest in Mythology and Lore of the 8 major Deity Pantheons, people who want a real MOBA with little salt and high challenge, or trying something new and exciting. Even if you're here just to watch the fights, it's worth the download time and worth the trial.

A little disclaimer here; I've bought and played this game before it came to Steam, and thus I know a bit more about what I'm doing, so my review may be a bit biased. To start us off, I'm going to list the pros and cons of the game.
Pros:
+Plenty to do. I've played on a single world for a looooong time, and only got around 3/4 to 4/5 through the game. I've never felt bored, and always had something to do.
+Fairly easy to predict what objects will do. For those of you who've played games like Minecraft, the basic mechanics of the game should be pretty easy to pick up.
+Automation. No, I DON'T want to mine for the whole game. I'd rather build machines to do it for me, and even more to make it go faster.
+Flexibility. There's no 'correct' way to make your giant monstrous contraptions, but there's always a better way.
+Exponential Growth. Remember when you had just one mining machine and one furnace? Yeah, I don't either.
Cons:
-Music is kinda boring, and Sounds can and will become repetitive quickly. I recommend muting the music in general and using your own.
-The enemies just won't stop. They keep coming and coming, so you'll need to constantly restock your turret's ammo (up until a certain point in the game), or automate that which takes resources. It may give you something to do, but it's just too frequent.*
-You might want to look at someone playing this or the Wiki before you jump in for more of the advanced stuff. Otherwise, the tutorial campaign's got you covered.
A Bit of Both:
/Enemy progression. If you've built a radar, it will eventually show where the enemy pods are in red. This is where they are coming from, so if you destroy them, you can stop enemy attacks entierly. The problem is, this and a few other factors (including pollution) causes them spawn stronger enemies, meaning there isn't a correct tactic for dealing with the problem. However, this allows for a more flexible and changing experience.
/Research. Yes, researching is fun to do, but eventually it needs to be completely automated, and the difficulty of the recipies makes automatic research hard for some and slow for others. Still, this issue doesn't arise until green or blue research is required.
/Finate resources. This forces you to expand your base far beyond what it's original size was, but this type of thing shouldn't be artificial.*
*Settings can be used to alter this feature.
All in all, the game's worth the 20$ I paid for it, even in it's early access form. It is perfectly playable, and the only downside is the lack of enemy variety. The rest of the game could be sold as a full release immediately, and has enough in it to surpass most similar games's value. So if you're looking for a game with elements from Terraria, Minecraft, Command & Conquer (or similar RTS games), Steampunk, and Tycoon games, then Factorio is the right choice for you.

While the story progression and general controls stay true and improve on Dark Souls, the newer game mechanics are where this game falls short of expectations.  Shields have been made all but obsolete by the guard break mechanic, which allows a character with no strength to push the heaviest shields in the game aside as if they were nothing, not only destroying the viability of heavy builds, but also leaving the player with the feeling that something just doesn't sit right in the Dark Souls universe.
In addition to this, the soul memory mechanic, that is where matchmaking is based on the total number of souls you have collected throughout the game, not on your character's level, not only destroys any semblance of fairness that the franchise once clung to, but also punishes you for not levelling up your stats to the maximum amount allowed;  Sooner or later you will die and you will lose your souls, if you didn't spend them on levelling up, that's just tough.   All this does is cause every build to become practically identical.  Where flaming katanas were rampant in Dark Souls, Dark souls 2 has replaced them with top level builds wielding high int/faith spells, heavy weapons and heavy armour, because not only is there no penalty for equipping all of these things, the game actively encourages it.
Finally, the first of the DLC trilogy, despite it's relatively low cost is short and underwhelming.  Much of the content feels recycled and as a whole it left me personally feeling confused and somewhat conned.
In short, if you enjoyed Demon and Dark souls, you will probably enjoy this, but you may find yourself wanting for more when it is all over.

If you read my Dark Souls:PTD review you'd probably know I said it suffers greatly from grinding as a main way to slam challenge into the game via eating at the players lack of patience, as the character has stats lower than every single NPC at every given time.
I recommended the game anyway, as it's still really good.

Well, this game is more of the same, in some respects, but let me explain why it's not a grind-fest.
First off, if you kill any enemy more than 10 times (Or maybe 20), it stops spawning in. This means, you can't reliably grind one single spot for eternity and get so powerful you can two-shot the boss via time-sink strategies. What this also means, is that the enemies are far more easy to fight, if you played the first game, this game is easy. In a lot of ways this is more of the same. If enemies are weak to an element or tactic, chances are, the game will leave subtle hints in the item drops and the enemy design on how to get past a specific challenge. (The first game also did this, but it is done consistently well here.)
Some other noticeable improvements though:
You get pushed off cliffs via narrow paths less,
Status effects are more bearable so they are more frequent, and easier to fit into builds.
Armor and weapon variation and possibilities are in the millions of combinations.
Equipment is harder to upgrade (Yes this is actually a plus, for the same reason less grinding is a plus).
Rings are more useful.
NPC's are more interesting.
Items look cooler (Most popular old items are still in the game, actually).
Level design is even better.
Bosses are harder to fight.
Kiting becomes almost impossible as areas are often less open.
Dex based dual-wielding characters are challenging and fun as ♥♥♥♥ to play (where dual-wielding wasn't a viable tactic in the last game due to lack of decent move-set options).
Here's the technical parts that are improved, as Dark Souls:PTD had a rather ♥♥♥♥♥♥ PC port:
Runs at 60fps without mods.
Keyboard and mouse actually rather pleasing to use compared to controller in some aspects, especially in menus.
Playing with friends is now possible, as long as you are both around the same level and have a specific ring, the game still prioritizes people you've summoned before.
The game has bind-able keys, which is always a plus for me.
This game is better in every way compared to the first. The only thing I miss is Sir Artorias and his wolf, Sif.

is an atmospheric game where you'll be guided by the echo of your footsteps to find a way out. It's visually simple, but the color scheme is enough to make you feel like you're actually in a dark room. The screams when you die and the weird sounds enemies make are enough to create a little bit of tension on us.
The game is cheap and it can be a distraction when you have nothing else to do. It also has achievements and trading cards, so completionists (like me) might enjoy it.
I found its premise to be deceiving. I have read, on both store page and news, that the game turned sound into gameplay, which is not true. Playing on mute or without headphones makes absolutely no difference. I was expecting something where I could play with my eyes closed and be guided by my ears, but all I had to do was look at the lines on the ground.
Its puzzles aren't exactly puzzles. Everything you need to do is walk around, find some switches (I've always found them before I even knew there was a closed door), hide from enemies or run from them. The most thinking you'll need is to decide when to walk and when to sneak.
It doesn't live up to its horror categorization. You don't even get to know what the enemies are. It's not a bad game, I was just... expecting something else.
Game encourages a bunch of sneaking :/ I don't like sneaking.

For being such a short game, it's worth playing it for it's price.
The sound design is spot-on, from the echoing footsteps to the sound of water droplets, giving the game it's perfect claustrophobic atmosphere. It's level design reinforcing this atmosphere even further with narrow hallways, small rooms, and even deadly little bridges. It's not even a horror game, but instead more of a puzzle game. If you think it's more a horror one then go ahead, we won't judge!
The game's mechanic itself about revealing your surrounding through sounds makes for some interesting puzzles and challenges, although it becomes a bit repetitive on later levels. It still remains fun nonetheless!
Overall, this is one solid and fun game to play. It may be short, but it's still a blast trying to sneak past the monsters and solving puzzles!

Creative, unique, repetitive and boring...
I was really looking forward to playing this one, since I enjoy exploring unqiue games that introduced new gaming mechanics.  Unfortunately, the idea itself is the best part.
The game is visually interesting, even though it is very simplistic.  That, along side the sound design creates an immersive experience, unfortunately that experience is not very exciting, nor interesting.
A game like this really has a great opportunity to slowly introduce new and more interesting/challenging gaming mechanics, but this one just does more of the same, over and over.  I was bored after the first few levels and the rest became tedious...Another of those games you just cannot wait until it is over :(
Good game design does not mean "filler" levels...This is a case of wanting the game to end, since there is nothing to look forward to, but there were way too many repetitive levels implemented.  It really feels just like simple mazes that you can only see from the reflected sound waves, just not very fun.
ACHIEVEMENTS:  Simply play the game...There are 15 hidden treasures to collect as well.

A fair warning: this game will take a particularly long time to download, perhaps even a total over 24 hours.  Even after you download it on Steam, it's going to take a while for the game to download all of its patches and updates with its launcher.  However, such a long download time in no unwarrented.  This game is jam packed with content inculding huge detailed worldspaces populated with fully voiced characters, so it makes since to have such a big file size.
Overall, I really like this game.  It's got hundreds of hourse of gameplay, and it's set in my favourite fantasy realm.  Although it's not quite the same as playing one of the single player Elder Scrolls games, it's still the best MMO I've ever played.  And the first one I've played that doesn't feel like a WoW clone.
Although, it isn't without a few drawbacks.  The most notible of which being that the fully voiced characters are a bit of a hit and miss.  Some of them are actually really good, but others are entirely unfit castings, and some of them make me wonder how on Nirn these people thought it would be a good idea to pursue a career as a profesional voice actor at all, or how anyone in their right mind thought it was a good idea to cast such people as hundreds of NPCs to be heard by millions.
Another drawback is that combat is more about your character's power and stats, and less about your skill as a player.
Still it's a delightful game, and if you want to try to get into an MMO, this is the one.

Enslaved – Odyssey to the West
Enslaved is one of the most underrated games ever. I really have no idea why this game  performed poorly sales wise. The only thing I can think of is that it was inadequately promoted – Namco Bandai pretty much acknowledge that too.
Anyway don't let the fact that you heard little about it put you off - I can tell you it really is a great game - one of the best games I have ever played IMHO.

The game was loosely based on a Chinese Novel but differs from the the original story which set a fantasy version of ancient China, to a post-apocalyptic world some 150 years in the future where human existence is sparse and hard. Only scattered residues of humanity remain but left over war-mechs roam the land, still active from the previous global conflict. The plot revolves around Trip (Tripitaka) a captured slave (and tech wizard) who forces the help and protection of a warrior type 'Monkey', who himself is enslaved. They both escape a sabotaged slaver air-ship and 'Monkey' the protagonist you play as, quickly finds himself at the mercy and control of Trip. Incidentally 'Monkey' is excellently voiced and performed by Andy Serkis (of Gollum fame) who was also Performance Director on the project. In fact all characters in this game are outstandingly portrayed and consequently very believable, this adds to the immersion of the game and story.
Anyhow, you discover Trip is wanting to return to her remote community and requires nay needs Monkey's help to get her there. There's an important twist here, as Monkey, you have little choice in the matter - you can discover the detail of why for yourself – and you are tied to her in an interesting way. You find that you often have to piggy back her to difficult to reach places and physically throw her to ledges and across gaps. Its sounds strange but its actually a neat mechanic. My small beef was there ought to have been even more requirement to control and this would have enhanced the experience and tightened the relationship you have with them as characters. I would also have preferred that you could have had an extended command structure both ways but like I said it is a minor niggle.
The fight mechanism is quite extensive and there were many ways I found to complete tasks and defeat enemies and the overall feel was rewarding and that goes for the Boss Fights too. While the story and scope to explore is limited it never really felt that way as in certain areas you had quite a bit of freedom to do things in your own style. Anyway visually, its great to look at too and all movement and animations are solid and fluid. For me, after only a short while you easily get to grow to like these characters and there's a real affinity you get for each of the characters plight.
I highly recommend this game and if you happen to see it in Steam Sales, I suggest you get it. I'm sure you wont be disappointed!

The Body Changer is a genuinely intriguing blend of genres: at its core, it's a third person puzzle metroidvania game. But then it also splashes in some tense action gameplay alongside for you to experiment with (and these scenes are pretty tense). The challenges get progressively harder as you complete the objectives, and you get to tinker about with more guns & gadgets as well. And that's before we get onto the fantastic 'body-switching' mechanic - which adds that extra bit of ingenuity to make it a really fun game.
It also provides a solid return to the metroidvania genre* (see below). Expect to be racking your brains to figure out the puzzles, going back on yourself, finding objects which you just can't quite lay your hands on ;)
Also worth mentioning is the backdrop story and notably the art-style, which help provide an authentic, other-worldy (and eerie) atmopshere.
So it has a lot of potential, and with its open-minded devs, hopefully the ideas streaming in from players should be realised to a great standard. I am not trying to over-hype this game (which is a bad thing!), but it really does show a lot of promise, and does a lot of things well.
+ Original blend of mechanics. Puzzle, action, themes from survival horror even. All encompassed by its evident dedication to the metroidvania genre.
+ Brilliant 'body-switching' mechanic. A lot of realised potential for this.. but there's more that's waiting to be explored with this I'm sure ;)
+ Great devs (only two of them as well!). They have a growing workload, yet they still remain in constant contact with their players. In my personal experience, they have only ever listened and acted on my feedback.
(Not directly to do with the game content, but hopefully should turn the faces of anyone put off by the 'Early Access' label)
+ Art-style is subjective to opinion (we might see some discussions arise in its Early Access stage), but I think it suits very well.
+ Weirdly eerie. Atmospheric and even frightening at the right times (there's that survival horror coming in!).. Decent SFX
+ Challenging puzzles & sticks true to metroidvania genre. You work out the puzzle (yes, it might be difficult!), and be prepared to go back on yourself a few times (a key mechanic of the metroidvania genre)
- Slightly clunky combat mechanics. These I'm sure will get a lot attention though.
- Environments could be a bit more .. pretty. In its current state. Minimalist world does suit though (complements the cel-shaded art-style).
- Some game progression bugs.
- UI needs a lot of work.
- Some QA (Quality Assurance) issues (relatively minor stuff though).
- Game could be longer (with more varied puzzles/combat sequences)... although it is by no means unimpressive at its current completion time (devs have said they are working on adding more levels).
- *EDIT: In my view, I would call this a solid metroidvania title.. however having read other reviews, some might think it doesn't do enough to earn that title. The game is likely to evolve more though to suit that genre if you felt it doesn't quite cut it.
- EDIT: Price. I would have imagined this as more of a below £10 (approx. $15) range title.
All in all though, this for me
been one of the most interesting games I've played for a while. Its setup very well by this original blend of mechanics, as well as reintroducing a dedicated and fitting return to the metroidvania genre.
The devs are great too - and rest assured you will be listened to! (Of course they are also very busy - but they have shown nothing but passion to deliver on this project!)
And yes.. I have temporarily renamed my display name in respect to the devs and the game :)

The Body Changer IMO feels like a Dead Space with less horror, simplier graphics, but harder and better puzzles.
I played the game in beta (around 0.5.9)
So far the game contains 5 sectors and roughly 3 hours of game time.
The Story is simple, almost non existence, but I didn't really miss it. The game focuses around the mix of puzzles with different elements, combat and the ability to switch characters with different abilities (and on different locations) to solve those puzzles. IMO it started out a bit slow, but from chapter 3 on I really had a lot of fun. The combat itself sometimes requires techniques to win, simple shooting won't always win. The puzzles are never unfair, yet sometimes challenging.
I am running this game with a AMD X2 4000+ with a ATI 4670 (toaster) and I could still run it on medium graphic settings without bigger problems.Only 1 passage with a lot of combat gave me FPS drops, but still playable. (with lower graphic settings no issue)
The game still has a lot to do imo. More content ofc and some optimization, and maybe it will develop its full potential, although I am not so sure about that since it has only 2 devs. As full potential I mean not just a working game that delivers, but also does some extra, like better told story, voice dubbing and maybe a coop one day. This would be a nice plus.
In general I see the devs are going into the right direction. They quickly answered to bug reports and fixed them so far.
As the game is atm I give it a 7/10.

I highly recommend this game. What stood out to me the most is that I didn't see the repeatitive copying of items, floor layouts, or cloned npc's (minus the robots). The station looked lived in. Each area felt unique and that it had a purpose or logic to it. Overall, the layout, the ambience, lighting, sounds and feel of the environment is the best I've ever seen in a sci-fi game.
An add bonus for me was when I bought the game I had an ok/older graphics card (it was like a radeon 6670 2gb ddr3). The game still looked beautiful on low settings.
The noise and sounds of the game... emerges you into the environment (recommend head phones for intensifying game experience). Sounds ranging from something metallic dropping in the distance and the droning hum of the station to the alien stalking you in the air vents.
Gameplay: Its a stealth/survival type game. It has elements of crafting, some combat if you get caught, small puzzle/problem solving situations. The alien AI will adapt to your habits of hiding so don't always go for the wall locker or rolling cabinet. There is more than one path to get around obsticals undetected... which can make it easier to remain undetected but may be the end of you if you linger to long.
Tip: USE THE LEAN ACTION! If your crouched behind an object you better be leaning against a wall or said object. Line of sight will get you 9 out of 10 but if your leaning you have an extremely higher chance of not being seen from peripheral vision.
You have a few moments in the game where you can move about the station freely without stiring unwanted attention. Thankfully it isn't limited to the beginning of the game.
Story: good story line. As far as I can tell, it keeps true to the movie and the world that was created by the movie. There are some parts (small parts) of the game towards the end that weren't realistic but its also a game and its fiction so... yeah. There is only one ending and its an open ended one... which is what you want to a good game so you can look forward to a sequel. IF they do... Which they should... Because I can't understand why they would not...
Reading from interviews with developers, they are WANTING to do a sequal but no official yes.
What was unexpected was that the jumpy parts of the game didn't involve the alien... I'll leave it at that.

I think this one is going to feel rather bad to write. Largely, because the free release was magnitudes better and this team clearly put their hearts into this amazing project.
I had followed the progress of Black Mesa for a very, very long time. Now some issues I had with the premium release have been fixed since, but I'll never
many of  those issues.
First, let's talk visuals. There's... Nothing wrong here. Everything, and I do mean everything, looks STELLAR. I mean, wow. There is nothing about Black Mesa that doesn't look like something freshly released for your PS4, or something. Its visuals are the very definition of "Peak of 2014 fidelity" and that's not an insult. To be able to push the Source engine that far is a real credit to the engine's capabilities. Everything looks and sounds right, and there is no doubt about it. These are professional developers a decade in the making.
Next, we need to tackle environmental ovehauls. I really have no problem with how they retooled the in-and-outdoors of Black Mesa, and it feels just as cohesive as it did in the late 90s. Black Mesa is a marvel of faithful yet innovative recreation from an environmental standpoint. Really, incredible job guys.
...But let's get into the bad parts.
1: The weapon sandbox is awful. Let's tackle the biggest one- if I were to ask you, "What was your main tool for dispatching vortigaunts?" your answer is PROBABLY gonna be either the Revolver, or Shotgun. Well, they both suck and shine. See, the revolver was a one hit kill for Vorts in ye-olde, no matter where you hit them.
It was a really great tool for taking out a threat at long range before it became a threat, but it has absolutely not stayed that way and is strictly only useful as a precision weapon that you use once or twice in a fight, because its rate of fire and its reload speed is absolutely dreadful.
The shotgun... Sometimes works, sometimes doesn't. When it 1HKs things when and where you expect it to, it's great. When it doesn't 1HK a Bullsquid at point blank using its alt-fire, suddenly you wonder where the hell your reliable shotty went, along with about thirty units of energy that you lost due to no real error of your own.
The SMG is simply put, overpowered. It used to be a bullet hose with a 45 round magazine and a really high-arc low velocity Grenade Launcher that, while on the surface was a bad weapon, actually became extremely potent in the right hands. I can tell you right now that if I were stuck with any single weapon from the original Half-Life and could pick, it'd be the SMG. But its lower magazine, higher damage and accuracy (at least, I THINK higher damage), and high velocity grenade launcher make the SMG an excellent tool for almost every situation, hampered only, ONLY by a shallow reserve ammo pool.
The Hivehand is better now, but was the absolute worst when this game released on Steam. It was the best gun in the game, because, strangely unlike the free version, soldiers would duck and cover, hoping the seekers would just go away. So you could just litter the air with these things and the soldiers would just give up- and it was true for the Alien Grunts too! They just... Didn't react! Now this has been fixed and the Hivehand feels right again, but that doesn't mean we should excuse such horrible mistakes that were overlooked for a premium release.
2: The performance is really bad.
My computer is pretty mid grade, I'll admit that right now. She's not quite all she used to be... But there's always some kind of visible stutter, there's, when a liquid texture must load (oddly), a stutter that occurs thrice, and well... It just isn't good. It just does not run buttery smooth, and I don't quite expect it to because not only is this a premium mod, it's running on an engine that simply isn't designed for this stuff, so I seriously can't tarry on about it too much. But I lost a lot of fights and had to reload very often thanks to this almost-always-mid-combat stutter. Not a good quality for a fast-paced Shooter.
3: The enemy design (and AI) isn't good/fair.
So, the human grunts have a schrodinger's brain. You have to assume they do and don't have an iota of intelligence, because sometimes they'll be absolutely handicapped and unresponsive, sometimes they'll be an omniscient god of war. (See: The encounter with the tank near sewage that FORCES you into
correct answer- entering behind the tank.)
The Alien Grunts... Are about as irritating as you'd expect.
The Vortigaunts are truly some of the worst! Sometimes their accuracy is terrible, but other times they can hit Buzz freakin' Aldren in orbit above earth if they so well pleased. On top of that, the revolver does not 1HK them like it should, so you're constantly searching for a mid-to-long range weapon that can quickly and effortlessly dispatch Vortigaunts, one of the game's most potent long range threats when other, more dangerous enemies are abound.
Lastly, the Icthyosaur. I still have nightmares about this animal, and I think I always will. Its presentation in Black Mesa was right out of a dream I'd had a damned day prior, and I shouted, "NO, NUH-UH, NO WAY" for a good thirty minutes at my desk playing the free release for the first time. But, I manned up, got in the cage (terribly physics at play there by the way, that will almost always leave you with nothing between the Icky and you) and... Was very disappointed by how easy it was to kill. Not only am I outswimming a sodding apex predator in its own domain, its attack is too slow for me to really be threatened by, on top of it ONLY requiring three crossbow hits to kill as opposed to four, making the encounter oh so much less threatening. The creature becomes a complete non-issue, and given its legacy and difficulty before, that's a huge, huge shame.
So... What am I trying to say with all this?
Half-Life and Black Mesa are very different games. One has always run well, had a great weapon and enemy sandbox, wonderful level design and has one of the longest standing legacies in gaming, on top of being an outright revolutionary title for its time.
Black Mesa is an almost perfect dish in its original release that somehow spoiled very, very quickly no more than a year later (and not coming out with Xen alongside the premium price.) Its premium release is worse than its free release in almost every conceivable way, and that's an incredible shame, because I called "Black Mesa" the definitive version of Half-Life everybody should play, instead of the original.
Now...
Now, I cannot say that.
I just hope Xen is good.

This vote addresses the full price of 20 euros. If you can get the game on sale like I did at 8 euros, then I recommend it. Otherwise, in the game's current state, no.
What do I mean by that? Weeyl, I am incredibly sad to say that this game is now considerably more buggy than it was a couple years back when I played the free version, which I believe is still available, mind you.
To start with, I have experienced numerous visual/graphical bugs, such as corpses falling through the ground, gliding through objects and out of the map, or just standing straight up. I swear, after I loaded a quicksave upon dying one time, the Vorts I killed were standing in line, upright, with arms outstretched, like Jesuses on crosses. What the hell that was I do not know.
Furthermore, on a more pertinent note, the AI is quite ♥♥♥♥ed in certain situations. For instance, as soon as I open the door to go outside and cross to the launch room to launch that missile in "On Rails," the soldiers in the far distance spot me instantly and open fire. I am crouching, mind you, and the two soldiers that are up close with their backs turned to me are ♥♥♥♥ing CHATTING WITH EACH OTHER about Freeman while their comrades riddle all of us with bullets from afar. I kid you not. I love this part since the old days, and I was excited to listen to the grunts talk about me once more while I plot my approach, but nope, it's impossible. I tried loading back two times too, but they had them wall hacks each time.
In general, the soldiers will sometimes rush you like blind men, coming up to you and just not firing for some reason, like they are lost or something. Had that happen at least three times so far. Keep in mind that I don't remember ever experiencing any of these issues back in the free version!
Bonus: The new shotgun model is absolutely hideous and needs to go ASAP. And removing radio chatter from soldiers was a bad idea. Granted, the over-the-top voice acting in the free version needed replacing, but removing it altogether really hurts immersion for me.
Yes, the game has multiplayer. The player base is tiny and it's completely normal not to be able to find a populated server during the day. But when you do, it can be pretty fun and hilarious in deathmatch, which is the only mode I played so far. That is until a hacker shows up, of course. After only a couple hours of playing this very scarcely populated game, I was faced with a haxor of biblical proportions; aimbot, walls and all. I reported him on Steam, cause there is no in-game option to do so. And while I was doing this, I took a peek at his profile comments to find that this dude has been hacking in Black Mesa for like 4+ months apparently with impunity.
So, until the game is polished and Xen is introduced, not worth 20 bucks by any stretch. 8 euros is more than reasonable, tho.
If the base price was like 10 euros, I'd have thumbed up.

Overall: Great game, would recommend to anyone who enjoys stealth or even general FPS games.
I'll be brief with this one:
Stealth Done Right - This game sets the bar for what good stealth games need to meet. The game incrementally improves on the previous Dishonored and does a great job of making the game difficult in interesting ways.
Combat - But if you like to fight, the fighting is fun as well. The sword combat is solid and fluid, though I imagine you'll spend most of your time hidden rather than in the spotlight. To each their own, though!
Level Design - This is what blows even Dishonored 1 away. The levels are beautiful, diverse, and a blast to route through. There's great diversity in what paths you can take and where you can go, even compared to the previous game.
Storyline - Another improvement from the previous game. Of course, the multiple endings are available, but the Outsider himself is fleshed out a lot more and the Void is given much more attention rather than the somewhat nebulous source of power it was in the first game. The characters remain well written as well, with their dialogue sounding natural and enjoyable. Also worth mentioning that Corvo's voicing is great as well - I found his voiced self more interesting than the silent.
Other - Difficulty is customizable like nothing you've seen before. You can adjust literally everything, between how attentive the guard's vision is to how much health potions restore. Picking between Corvo and Emily is neat too, and their power differences make for nice replay value. You can even do a power-less run if you desire a challenge.
Performance is Mediocre - I'll give credit where credit is due: the game looks great even on low-mid settings, and the patches since release have made performance better. Unfortunately, you'll still get frame drops in many areas, and the game still tends to run slowly otherwise.
The load times are also very long - I'm not sure if they were this bad in the first game, or what, but if you quick-load a lot (aiming for that ghost run, right?) the long load times become annoying.
This is a great game, period. I can recommend this almost universally - at least try it if you're on the fence. Anyone who enjoys stealth games ought to get this and anyone else might enjoy it regardless; this is *the* stealth game of the video game world.

My review of this game is way late, I realize, but it never dawned on me until now to do one. I thoroughly enjoyed the game as a whole. The gameplay was excellent and the story as well was good. I was surprised, to be honest. I was having trouble with how they could do a second game considering what makes Dishonored what it is. Corvo is 'dishonored' and blamed for an assassination he never committed and its a story of redemption. Doing that all over again seems a little silly. You would, at the very least, need a new antagonist with a different reason or motive for wanting the throne; not simply for political gain. Dishonored 2's antagonist is just that, in fact, she is family.
Even still, the idea of Corvo once again being dishonored and dethroned and tossed into essentially the same situation seems rather redundant at this point, and it makes it all the more compelling to play as Emily: Not to mention, it makes for an interesting dynamic to see how Emily, who is raised up and trained by her father, Corvo, would handle this kind of situation and how well all that training paid off; to see what happens when Emily cannot rely on her father to help her, she must do this herself, and of course, the fact that Emily has her own set of powers also makes it compelling to play as her. Nevertheless, in spite of the redundancy, there would still be good story development having Corvo in the protagonist seat again. Along with an amplified set of powers, Corvo has to save the heiress again, and the legend lives on.
The gameplay was smooth and gave me no trouble at all. The AI can be challenging on higher levels, and the gameplay, though not shunning direct combat engagement, certainly encourages tactical play. One can easily be overwhelmed by just two or three soldiers, and the clock-work soldiers were as challenging as they were fascinating to look at. The animations were very interesting to see. Much like its predecessor, this one allows multiple ways to complete objectives and of course, the option to not kill your target. Although I would love to see, not just two different options (kill or spare), but various ways to do those two options, it is nonetheless satisfying to know the choice is in our hands.
My biggest complaint has to do with the story. I thought it was short, and to be honest, though there were various ways to go about missions, the game couldn't help but feel redundant. I have played this game quite some bit.  I recently decided to knock it down to one night a week. Getting burned out.  ALl in all, I feel this is the best MMO out.
First the pros:  Big world, fights are fast paced and veteran level content is unforgiving for those who like to not dodge mechanics.  The graphics are beautiful for it's age.   Community as a whole is great.  Most people are very very helpful and nice (although getting them to talk with a mic is like asking them to swallow glass!).  The population of the community feels great after 1 tam came out.
Now the cons.  There are a ton of bugs in the game.  None that are game breaking, but they do get annoying.  Customer service is a joke.  Bad class balancing.  Used to be magic based characters were overpowered.  Now it is the stamina based versions of the same classes.  The downfall is all the stam based characters feel VERY generic and lack uniqueness (literally 80% of stam based skills are the same across classes).  The magic based characters feel much more unique in their abilities, but their performance took a big hit after Dark Brotherhood (you can play them, but there is a noticable difference).  When it comes to loot, it literally are running the same content over and over and over and over hoping your piece drops with the right configuration on it.  The content for me, got old quick after clearing vet material.  You are basically reduced to a chimp pulling a lever 500 times for a piece of candy.  Some people really like the PVP, but it wasnt for me.
Hopefully this helps you decide if it is right for you.  If you like MMOs, and dont expect Skyrim!, check it out.  I think you will pleasantly surprised until the you eventually get bored.  That will take awhile though!

For fans of Scott's seminal 'Alien', a must. Attemtps ardently to evoke the retro-futurism and grimy schtick of late-70s sci-fi  with great success. Beautiful to look at, atmospheric. Unbelievable sound design. Well optimised. I really love the control scheme - leaning around corners or cover is encouraged, and necessary.
The first four or five hours on Sevastopol station are credible and tense; once introduced, the xenomorph is frightening and ominous. Never have I felt so
as a player character. The level design during these hours is complicated, and there are many places to hide, although not all are safe. Playng cat and mouse with the alien is dynamic and arresting. Unfortunately as the game progresses and the need to conceal one's self lessens, the level design becomes less intricate, populated with human and android obstacles that never match the unpredictability and cunning of the xenomorph AI.
The plot is simplistic, and can be surmised as 'You're stuck on a deteriorating space station, stalked by psychotic androids and a terrifying pradator. Do find a way out, much. And any traces of your mum's lost vessel, those are good too.' Viewed from this distance I was able to pleasantly engage in the simulation of being imprisoned and looking for a way out, piecing together and gathering what tools I could. Ripley's search for her mother takes a back seat, regrettably, and I do wish more was made of this - the imperative which beckoned her to Sevastopol in the first place. Going out of her way to discover recordings from the Nostromo's crew seems completely at odds with the primal instinct to find the nearest exit.
I enjoyed embodying Ripley as a scared but resilient engineer with a good dose of humanity, and whilst the late game's devolution into sparser designs and less exciting enemy encounters hamper the game, I strongly recommend it.

I've been playing this since it's release on Desura.
Looking back "The Body Changer" kept evolving at a steady pace most early access titles lack, ever after their official steam launch.
Quite an impressive development for an indie game that is programmed by just two guys from italy ^^
But what really shapes a game in the making, is a steady dialog with the community and the first adopters.
Considering that a constumer wants to be taken serious and to get involved in the process, the developers nailed it.
So, what ist "The Body Changer" all about?
You wake up in a futuristic facility as sort of an synthetic being called SynB who is able to transport his "mind" into other SynB each with it's unique abilitys and powers.
Some can cross barriers that are harmful to others while some are masters of gun and hand to hand combat.
Your task is to stop an unknown contamination of the facility systems that infects most of the other SynB and causes them to go on a ramapge.
You move your protagonist through the stylized and futuristic hallways and server rooms of the facility in third person view.
On your way you encounter different kind of puzzles which force you to combine the different attributes of the SynB you can control.
Switching between items and SynB characters is done via radial menus which is very comfortable. Moving, running, using and combat moves follow the genre standards, so there is no steep learning curve if you played other third-person action adventures.
The graphic are simplistic with a sleak cell-shading look to it. They transport the feeling of being alone in a abandoned facility very well and are rather unique.
If TheShortAndTheTall keep in touch with their community, I'm sure the final incarnation will come around nicely in the end.

In terms of graphical fidelity, this is one of the best remasters out there. Gearbox and the rest really outdid themselves. They pulled all sorts of original staff and voice actors out of the woodwork. It's very faithful to the original look, it performs well and it looks damn good.
It also includes the original games, completely unmodified. This is the only legal way to acquire them digitally. In all honesty, the original version of the first game is well worth $30 and I have no regrets about my purchase. Keep that in mind when reading the following.
As a Homeworld 1 purist, the remaster of that game has a few problems. A lot of it behaves more like HW2 than classic HW1. Strike craft won't stay in formation, research costs resources, fuel has apparently been removed, and multiple mechanics have been switched from true physics to simple probabilities. You don't have nearly as solid or immediate control over your ships as you had in HW1, and everything feels slightly abstracted. The UI was switched to the HW2 model as well, which is jarring. It's not objectively worse, it's just very different.
All in all, it doesn't quite play like HW1. It plays like a very pretty, very well-made HW1 port mod for HW2 - which is precisely what it is.

Compared to other big MOBAs and ARTs out there, SMITE is one of the 3 well established giants in the industry. It is more casual than Dota with fewer complex mechanics and being more user friendly and easier to get into. Compared to LoL I would say this game is more immersive. It is much more fun (in my opinion) with a much bigger percentage of characters being viable and fitting the 'meta'. SMITE's lore is really interesting too, it being based on Gods and Immortals from different mythologies and it curious how Hi-Rez mixes all the pantheons together.
Gameplay-wise there are 7 gamemodes as of now, so plenty to play and choose from. Conquest - the traditional 5v5 map with 3 lanes and jungle. Joust - 3v3 with one lane and smaller number of jungle camps. Arena - 5v5 in a colosseum with one wave of creeps marching down and the win condition being ticket based. Assault - another common gamemode with all-random God selection and one lane and no fountain to return to (similar to ARAM in LoL). Clash - 5v5 with 2 lanes and I really don't know what the ♥♥♥♥ is going on in this one. Siege - 4v4 with 2 lanes and jungle in the middle. MOTD - Match of the day, chosen by the devs themselves, this gamemode can be ridiculous or boring, it can be 5v5 of the same God with max money or just a vanilla gamemode, but with cooldown reductions. Overall, you will never be bored with such a range of casual gamemodes in addition to ranked Conquest, Joust and Duel.
This is a fun game, better with friends, you can play casually or try-hard. There are regular patches and events, and new Gods being released almost monthly.
P.S. Invest into an All-Gods pack if you decided to play the game long term, it saves you a lot of money with every month as you get new Gods at their release.

I've played most of the free MOBAs out there, save one Heroes of The Storm. I simply refuse to touch it or any other MOBA after finding this gem.
To start from the beginning, I was avoiding MOBAs quite a bit at first. Having a game simply revolved around 2 teams of players beating the everloving hell out of each other seemed pointless to me at first, but it was soon that I would try DOTA2 - and find out that these games have a certain charm to them that make them entertaining to watch and play. Much like how sports-fanatics religiously watch football, basketball, etc, MOBAs are as such to the people of the internet who love watching fantasy heroes beat the hell out of each other.
It was also with this that I learned where the toxic wastes of the internet thrive, as MOBAs tend to have huge pools of crude, cruel, salty trolls, the most toxic people to exist. You can't join one game without finding anywhere between 2-5 people who can't help but call you any of the worst things on the planet and demanding you to kill yourself in a fire.
Enough about those toxic cesspools though because it was this little gem, SMITE, that gave me insight that not all MOBAs are filled with the worst kind of people in internet history. There are people you just want to kill yes, but it's a huge decline in toxicity compared to most MOBAs (in comparison to DOTA 2 90% less cyanide is being ingested daily when playing SMITE).
The game itself is brilliant in every aspect of the word, while majority of MOBAs have you at a top-down visual and using your mouse to 100% control the character you choose, SMITE allows you to not only control the God you select, but become them, and using every aspect of their ability with the precision and skill they require to be good with them. The game is also 100% totally free, not requiring you to access any form of paywalls for any of the content. Gems, the current cash-like currency, is free to gain in the game through events, promotions, and daily logins, as well as through referring and playing with friends.  All Gods can be obtained with Gems or Favor earned through gameplay, as well as all skins and costumes in the game. The only thing using real world money will do is get you the Gods and skins faster.
Revisiting the community subject, the community in SMITE is very close together. You have a few bad eggs and salty trolls here and there, but as I said before in comparison to other MOBAs, or any MMO for that matter, the number is relatively low, and you can happily play most games without overdosing on your daily sodium intake.
The controls are very intuitive, in my experience, including Keyboard/Mouse and Gamepad support and allowing for easy gameplay no matter what kind of game peripherals you're used to. I personally play with Keyboard and Mouse, as that is what I'm used to using for precision aiming, which brings me to the gameplay mechanics. In many Mobas aiming is as easy as pointing and clicking on the ground or another player, but in SMITE you are expected to be able to aim properly with most abilities. Eat your heart out LoL's Ezreal. This game requires you to pay attention and aim your shots wisely. Some require less skill than others (Kukulkan's Whirlwind), while others require you to line them up nicely for a good result (Neith's Spirit Arrow). There are no ingame boosts to get you ahead of the game's curve or "Pay 2 Win" systems - SMITE wants you to experience the entire game for what it is at its fullest. For that, I give Hi-Rez studio an amazingly large thumbs-up.
Wrapping up this long read of a review, I totally recommend this game to anyone who has an interest in Mythology and Lore of the 8 major Deity Pantheons, people who want a real MOBA with little salt and high challenge, or trying something new and exciting. Even if you're here just to watch the fights, it's worth the download time and worth the trial.

I'm going to review the Single player portion of the game since the overwhelming number of reviews here appear to be for the multiplayer and are already negative
Considering how poorly the multiplayer has been reviewed here it is unfortunate the Single player cannot help to prop this iteration of the series up.
The Good
Beautiful, diverse, eclectic, detailed maps
Fantastically detailed character models and excellent animation
Interesting & novel new weapons & enemies
Suprisingly robust video/control customization options
The bad
Extremely linear game play
No character customization  / exo suit power selection
Relatively short
Weak moralizing / increasingly weak story
No weapon stats / info
Occasional complete crashes / extreme FPS drops
Let me elaborate. Graphics look fantastic, character models are fantastic, most primary voice acting is very good too. Unfortunately prepare to be nagged to death by your NPC team mates. Deviate from the script for more than even 2 or 3 seconds and except to either be insta-killed, insta-fail the mission, or have your teammates remind you incessantly in an angry inpatient voice what you should be doing.
Maps look great however you never have the option to explore them, if there is anything to even explore. Either your shown a very pretty but elaborate on rails corridor or are hit with the Leaving Mission Zone
Exo Suits, drones, crazy weapons wow right!? Except you never get an opportunity to pick your load out during the entire game. Its pre-picked for you. Even still you do not have control over all your exo abilities usually only be allowed to use certain ones at the scripts insistence and never again.
Had some technical glitches, of course these vary for everyone  - running a 980 GTX  32 gig RAM  SSD. Usually framerate with most high settings was very good though occasionally it would crawl to almost a stop but then be fine on a subsequent or previous play through. Occasional hard crashes also.
Advanced Warfare Single player feels like an extended demo for what could be a truly awesome game. Of course what it really is a demo for a multiplayer game that at the moment is lacking strong numbers of players on servers. It is still disappointing though that after so many sequels in the CoD series that the story is still relatively lacking if not weaker then previous installments.
I recommend waiting till the game is well on sale, the current Season pass cost of $50 plus $60 for the base game is insane unless you are a hardcore COD multi player.

This game is a diamond in the rough. It has one of the most interesting settings I've ever seen and the character development is phenomenal. The voice acting in particular is some of the best in all of video games. The only real downside is that gameplay is as standard as you can get. The level design is reminicent of Devil May Cry but the platforming is contextual, meaning there is only one real way to go and is impossible to fail. There is some form of collectible hunting but it is mostly tied to the upgrade system, makeing it almost just as needless.
The gameplay in the DLC would have better suited the entire game, with abilities unlocking via progression and the game presenting you with a problem and expecting you to resolve it with what you have at your disposal. All in all, as someone who values story, setting and Immersion over gameplay, this game is pure gold and comes highly recomended. Indeed even considering the lack luster gameplay, I was completly won over by the charm and richness of the setting and story.

Enslaved: Odyssey to the West is a very good, but somewhat flawed game that deserves to be played by anyone who likes action-adventure-platformers. This game reminded me a lot of the Prince of Persia game from 2008. You do a fair amount of easy platforming and also spent a pretty good amount of time in combat. The combat is by no means difficult and by no means super interesting.
What makes the game work is that it does the few things it does very well. The platforming is solid and has great controls. I found myself enjoying all the little platforming sections they threw at me. They make the next object you are to leap to flash so you never find yourself wondering where to go next. Also, the combat in this game responds well. You are able to upgrade yourself as you play and I found that the extra costumes that came with this version of the game were really useful.
What does not work in this game are the turret sections. I found aiming the turrets in this game to be a chore and that it was really hard to hit moving targets enough to kill them. Obviously, I made it through the game, but I dreaded every time I was in a turret section. Fortunately, there are only about three or four turret sequences. I quit once, confident that I would be fine, only to come back and learn I had to replay 10-15 solid minutes. Annoying. The "surf board" sections are also annoying, but quite brief.
The laziness of the PC port is obvious at times. There are graphical glitches and I once had to reduce the game to the lowest resolution for the character to make a jump. Odd.
A final note about a few high points of the game. The characters and story are really good, as are the graphics. I found myself really liking both the main leads and was very much pulled into their adventure. The voice-acting is top notch and the facial capturing they did for these characters is one of the best in any game I've seen. The environments  are lush and beautiful and the game ran smoothly for the most part(aside from a few glitches).
In the end, I loved the game and really recommend it if you liked any Prince of Persia game.

Most people would say that Broforce's strength lies in it's fusion of Metal Slug style run-and-gun with the sheer chaos that comes from its constant chain reactions of gigantic explosions and destructible terrain along with the huge, diverse cast of characters, each equipped with unique and completely over-the-top firepower.
They may also say that the equally huge and diverse cast of enemies allows for interesting encounters, especially as the enemies grow more and more ridiculous alongside the plot (which also grows more and more ridiculous).
Many people may say that Broforce's mechanic of tying extra lives to switching your character compels players to unleash their hugely destructive secondary weapons regularly, lest they lose that ammo once they switch over to the next Bro they've rescued. These people would probably suggest that this mechanic elegantly contributes to those mentioned chain reactions of gigantic explosions and destructible terrain, essentially demanding that the player turn every firefight into an absolute mess of total carnage.
In the end, these people would hold that this points right to the true strength of Broforce: A well-tuned system guaranteed to create unpredictable Rube Goldberg machines of blood, explosions, flying propane tanks, falling rocks, and plenty of bullets inside plenty of terrorists. While there may be lots of unforeseen consequences that would force you to restart your level over and over, these people would say that this only helps the game's case - even your deaths in Broforce are as ridiculous as your kills.
Unfortunately, these people would be wrong. Broforce's strength lies in the chat system that lets you send action movie one liners on demand.

I have been playing the game for about 3 weeks now and just used my key they emailed me to add the game to steam.
I have also been active in reading the forum on their official site as well.  I Know this game as a huge following so please understand that this is a review of MY own experience with this game.
I really wanted to like this game. At first I got really excited! I generally love games that have deep mechanics and offer the player several different ways to accomplish tasks. However, I have found that the game is a bit to much micro management.
Now here me out. I understand that you can automate everything. But to do so you have to mine and set up machines and connections generally through conveyor belts and electric poles. The first time I got something working it was a good feeling of accomplishment. But from that point on it felt like a rinse and repeat. So when I say micro management, I mean that to me it feels like to much work and management just to set up everything to run automatically as it takes an insane amount of time to do so.
Im constantly doing the same things. Yes, the outcome might be a different "part" like making a lab to spit out research or getting my fluids build more compact. But in the end I realize that I was'nt really having any fun. The game just felt like work. I feel like im at a job. The game drags on. I enjoy when my base get's attacked so I decided to increase the difficulty, ie: making enemy bases bigger, more rich, and more bases but found that the game was not really challenging at all. Yes, the start was just a tad more difficult but once you get lasers attached to a power source then I felt like i had won the game!
Not to mention, that almost everytime my base would get attacked it would happen while I was somewhere else on the far side of my base "working" and I would not even see the attack. Just making me feel like I was missing out on the true fun. All and all at the end of the day after I did all that work I come to find out that once you launch this 1 rocket into the sky the game just ends. :/  Which brings me to the lackluster goal or lack of any goals. I really began to feel like I was doing everything for no reason. If you are not working on making your factories run smoother or more compact, which just brings the game to an end faster, than there really does not seem like there is anything else to do.
From what I noticed from my 3 weeks is that the game does well at holding a player hostage by forcing them to build these enomrous factories that again just feel like work to me. Now with that being said I dont have any friends to play multiplayer with. I do imagine the game would be more fun with 2 or more people as there are things like a car and tank where I imagine exploring with someone and killing the enemy bases would be enjoyable. But doing so by myself was not.
I do for some reason actually adore the graphics! I love the look of the character model and like how he changes as you upgrade the armour. I also love the aliens and think the dev's did a fantastic job on them as well. I just wish more of the game was focused on the interactions the player as with them and less on having to build massive factories.
I know the game is well recieved and I can see why, if your big into building and puzzle games you will probably love it! I say puzzle games because to me this felt a lot like a puzzle game where the object was to get things working in the most compact and efficient way possible. But to me that was just a feeling of work and ultimatley was not enough fun to hold my attention.
I will also add that I was amazed that this game is coming to steam as an early access title because I found that what the game does offer is extremly polished! I personally cant say that I ever ran into any bugs. The developers are wonderful from what I have seen in the forums and I will still be keeping and eye on this game and any future game this team makes! They have a great sense of humor as can be seen on their official website forum. I especially love the the post with the gifs depicting the devs as they work on things! Great post!
