In season 4 of smite, the balancing has been highly questionable. New characters such as artio and cu chulain come out as meta breaking and do not recieve the nerfs to bring them out of top tier picks. Other changes to gods have also been extremely questionable with changes as ullrs axe and fenrir recieving buffs changing the freedom the balanced wolf had in each situation in exchange for buffs to his already powerful abilities. Smite also has issues in items in the game, especially with items like gladiator shield which has influenced the solo lane since it became popular earlier this season. However, with each patch Hi-Rez makes changes that hurt the game more than help and do not make the changes offered by the community even though they offer a pts.
Smite also has performance issues. Along with a long loading time, I have been unable to even connect to the games I queue for, harming my team and myself for queueing at all. All I know that I can currently play the game without any problems in performance if I go into a bot match without anyone.
Overall these problems really just make me want to not play. While the game still holds the charm that it had almost 2 years ago, it reallly is not worth playing anymore. For 1500 hours, I have gotten the worth from the game. However, I have worries that Hi-Rez is pushing their game into the dirt for money(ULLLRRRR) and while the performance may be an issue with me, smite is currently the only game I cannot run fully while other games like league I run well. If you are interested in smite, do not buy anything immediatly and pay close attention to community responce for season 5, for it could be the nail in the coffin for smite

This is the game for all true hardcore Alien and survival horror fans. This is NOT a shooter. This is NOT a fast paced game. This is NOT a game you're going to get through in one (or even a few) sitting(s). This is a very slow paced, hide and seek thriller in the setting of the first Alien move.
Note: The game has a number of graphical and gameplay bugs, and the developers have dropped support for the game.

One of the better horror games I've played in years. Note that the game isn't scary so much as it is tense. The constantly changing nature of the AI keeps you on your toes and uncertain when the alien is around, and generally feels very cat-and-mouse. Controls are simple, but serviceable. The crafting system feels a little bit tacked on, but aside from that, the game is incredibly immersive. That retro-futuristic aesthetic from the films is absolutely nailed in the aesthetic design of this game from the CRT monitors down to many original ideas that you could swear would be right at home in any of the films. Very polished, a bit longwinded but decent value for the price.

The highest praise I can give this game is that it's how I
Half-Life. If you put this in front of me in another ten years, I might not even realise that I wasn't playing the original game.
The Source engine used by Black Mesa is showing its age in some respects - levels load frequently, many models (especially the humans!) are slightly odd-shaped, and the physics can be really unpredictable. It's a little grating when you come from a more recent game - especially considering that this game is still being worked on - but it's still a long way ahead of the game it remade.
This would be a fine way to experience Half-Life for the first time, but it stands up even better as a way to re-experience the original. The game was full of fond memories of the original (and some not-so-fond ones - I'm looking at you, assassins), especially as I came across new areas, weapons, enemies or game mechanics for the first time. Again.
I'm not sure if I'm looking forward to the Xen levels or not. The game holds up well without them, but they certainly weren't a highlight of the original Half-Life.

So, I finally decided to spend my whole Saturday playing the game after already having it in my library for a while now, and boy I have to say this game is AMAZNG. I'll make bullet points to make it easy to read.

- Combat: Very simple, it was meant to be for all gamers, bad and good ones, really easy to pick up.
- Music: Every soundtrack was different, and different in a good way, some were calming and nice, some were fit for the scene, overall really good.
- Art: very impressed by the art work as well as graphics. Art work was cute, adorable. Graphics was good, nostalgic to those old ARPGs, I actually appreciate that since I've only been playing AAA games lately, this was such a good change.
Overall, I really love the game, it gave me the "feels", definitely would cry again??? haha
If there was a sequel, I would want it to be a little longer, with a bit more complexity, and I WOULD pay for the sequel.

To the few people this applies to - forget everything good I've had to say about Dishonored 2. Even the best game is worthless if it's literally unplayable, and Dishonored 2 is precisely that, due to the Denuvo DRM. There are workarounds, but they imply things I don't intend to ever imply to a third party. To elaborate -
I played the entire Emily Kaldwin campaign of Dishonored 2 (stealth/mostly lethal), and then had the audacity to increase my system RAM without notifying Denuvo. Now, clearly this just wouldn't do, at least for them. They expect me to send them a notification through their DRM software every time I make a hardware change. Every single time. For free. Obviously I'm not about to take any action that implies that I'm alright with this arrangement, so they're not getting a single bit of data from me that I can avoid giving them (other than indicators that I don't accept, or even condone their terms), and that's why I'm locked out of a game that I already paid for. And already authenticated once through their proposterous DRM software, which I was frankly blindsided by the first time, and not nearly so much now. It's worth pointing out that Steam itself is a DRM software, and every other Bethesda and/or Arkane game sold through Steam has opted out of extraneous DRM for what (I assumed) was an obvious reason.
I bought a game from someone who isn't Denuvo (but evidently signed some type of deal with them), only to have Denuvo demand updates on my system changes for free, for a game that I've already authenticated through both Denuvo DRM and Steam, and have had installed for months, and played for over 30 (logged) hours. If I don't comply (which obviously I won't), I'll never get to play the game again. And it's made for a garish exploitation of the refund timeframe loophole. I won't be able to get a refund for a game in which I can't even reach the title screen anymore. Don't let them do the same to you. I appologize to anyone who decided to buy this game due (at least in part) to my previous review. Keep clear of Dishonored 2, and be very cautious about anything Bethesda and Arkane release on Steam in the future, and of Denuvo DRM.
